links.outcome: Readability of GPT outputs tailored to specified patient education level (health literacy proxy)
links.effect: GPT-3.5 met target readability only at bachelor's level; GPT-4 met target for all groups except 6th-grade FKRE. Clinical content accuracy was not evaluated.
links.quote: GPT-3.5 only aligned with the prespecified education levels at the bachelor's degree.

links.outcome: Consistency of readability across prompts varying only in stated patient education level
links.effect: GPT-4 outputs collapsed 6th and 8th grade into one tier with no significant difference; GPT-3.5 also failed to differentiate high school from bachelor's outputs.
links.quote: GPT-3.5 also demonstrated nonsignificant differences in readability between the 6th- and 8th-grade levels, both in individual DM scenarios and when considering the overall FKGL.

links.outcome: Whether generated patient text reading level matched requested user reading level
links.effect: GPT-3.5 6th-grade FKGL 9.08 and 8th-grade 10.27, above target; GPT-4 6th-grade FKRE 74.54, above target 6th-grade band (80-90 easy).
links.quote: GPT-3.5 only aligned with the prespecified education levels at the bachelor's degree.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of output readability across repeated runs
links.effect: Each scenario run 5 times; average FKRE SD 4.91 (GPT-3.5) and 4.86 (GPT-4); average FKGL SD 0.99 and 1.05, showing stable readability across repeats.
links.quote: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 demonstrated relatively consistent results in variability across all educational levels, suggesting that both versions of ChatGPT maintain uniform performance irrespective of the complexity of language in the clinical vignettes used.

links.outcome: targeted readability of patient education outputs
links.effect: GPT-4 accurate average readability in 13/16 scenarios; GPT-3.5 in 4/16, only bachelor’s degree.
links.quote: GPT-4 achieved accurate average readability scores in 13 out of 16 scenarios across both FKRE and FKGL, while GPT-3.5 reached accurate average readability scores in only 4 out of 16 scenarios, exclusively at the bachelor’s degree education level ( Tables 2 and 3 ).

links.effect: Average FKGL SDs were 0.99 for GPT-3.5 and 1.05 for GPT-4; roughly 95% within approximately two grade levels.
links.quote: Similarly, the average FKGL SDs were 0.99 for GPT-3.5 and 1.05 for GPT-4, indicating that roughly 95% of FKGL scores likely fall within approximately two grade levels, providing further evidence of output consistency.

links.effect: GPT-4 generally had higher FKRE/lower FKGL than GPT-3.5 except bachelor’s degree scenarios.
links.quote: This analysis suggests that GPT-4 generally delivered outputs with better readability (higher FKRE and lower FKGL) across various educational levels, with the exception of the bachelor’s degree scenarios ( Figures 4 A-6H).

links.outcome: Readability alignment with targeted patient education levels
links.effect: GPT-4 achieved accurate average readability in 13/16 scenarios, whereas GPT-3.5 achieved accurate readability in only 4/16 scenarios (bachelor's only). Aggregated 6th-grade FKGL was 6.3 for GPT-4 versus 9.08 for GPT-3.5.
links.quote: GPT-4 achieved accurate average readability scores in 13 out of 16 scenarios across both FKRE and FKGL, while GPT-3.5 reached accurate average readability scores in only 4 out of 16 scenarios, exclusively at the bachelor’s degree education level ( Tables 2 and 3 ).
